chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: First thoughts of music: four Barbarin uncles and the halls
summary: Growing up in the Seventh Ward among halls and four musician uncles, Danny heard constant talk about who could play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I just want to get back a little so we won't digress too far, Danny. When you were a kid around New Orleans, when did you first start to think about getting into music?

Well, I didn't think about it too much. I was going to school. And I'm hearing this music all the time, and I'd see these musicians, they're celebrated. I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin. We live in the neighborhood, in the Seventh Ward, where there's quite a few halls -- the (?) Hall, the Jean Ami Hall, the Franz(?) Ami Hall, the New Hall. And on Ledgerfield Avenue there was about four or five White halls. And there was music all the time. And I'm listening to the music...

And my uncles... My grandfather being in the brass band, he played the funerals with the Onward Brass Band, which was the greatest brass band at that time. And there was a rivalry between Manny Perez and George Moret(?), who was the leader of the Excelsior Band. And I'm hearing this. And my uncles, they're talkin' about who's who and who ain't. And it's a celebrate thing, and everybody is celebrated. So they would talk who could play and who couldn't, and who rated...
